parsed.reason: Strong on structure: it recommends the chair method plainly (playbook-backed for a toddler in a bed), gives stages with the playbook's every-3-nights fading, names the night 2-3 worsening as the old pattern breaking, includes a working signal, a doctor trigger, partner agreement, and a check-in day. But there are fabrications and gaps. 'Doctors Bjorkman (a pediatrician) have a good video' is an invented outside resource that isn't in the playbook, and that caps the score at 2. Other problems: the plan never says why the method is worth doing, never names Ferber as the alternative in a clause, and uses 'walk her back calmly' for the bed-leaving case, which the playbook doesn't spell out. It also calls the crib setup 'her own room' without addressing the existing bed-sharing situation, and it states the nights 7-9 schedule as if the playbook specified it, when the playbook only says every 3 nights or so.
